title: Change one condition
hook: A fair comparison keeps track of what changed.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy test of one sound cue, which design better isolates the cue: change only the sound, or change sound and food together?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In a toy test of one sound cue, which design better isolates the cue: change only the sound, or change sound and food together?

claims.text: In a toy test of one sound cue, which design better isolates the cue: change only the sound, or change sound and food together? The first comparison keeps the food the same and changes the cue; the second changes both sound and food. The first makes the sound contrast more interpretable, assuming other conditions are controlled and trials are repeated. This is a design, not a measured result.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
To test whether a light cue affects a choice, what should be held the same across the comparison? Holding relevant conditions constant helps isolate the manipulated cue.
